summary.oneLiner: Kansai Nerolac Paints Limited (KNPL), a subsidiary of Kansai Paint Co., Ltd., Japan, is one of India's largest paint and coatings manufacturers, leading the Automotive and Powder Coating segments and ranked third-largest in Decorative paints.
summary.business: KNPL manufactures and supplies paints, varnishes, enamels, lacquers, wood coatings, construction chemicals and tile adhesives across Decorative and Industrial (Automotive, Auto Refinish, Performance/Powder Coating) segments. It serves residential, commercial, industrial, government, institutional and retail customers in India, with automotive coatings supplied to 2-, 3- and 4-wheeler, electric vehicle, commercial vehicle and tractor OEMs, and industrial coatings to consumer durables, machinery and infrastructure applications.

Automotive Coatings: Underbody coatings, alloy wheel coatings, seam sealers
Auto Refinish: Refinish coatings for premium A-class body shops
Other end-use coatings: Consumer durables coatings (fans, microwaves, refrigerators, washing machines)
Personal items coatings (hair clips, artificial jewellery)

currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26, KNPL enhanced capacity at existing plants rather than adding new sites: water-based paints capacity was expanded at the Jainpur plant, and Cathodic Electro Deposition (CED) capacity was enhanced at the Sayakha plant, alongside internal initiatives to lift overall capacity through digital/automation investment. On the renewable-energy side, the Company commissioned a 2nd wind turbine of 2,100 KW capacity at Sayakha Plant, taking its captive windmill capacity to 10,500 KW (with windmill installations across Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat), and commissioned a 3,000 KW offsite captive solar farm in Yavatmal, Maharashtra, catering to power requirements at the Lote Plant — both pursued under the Company's 'Corporate RE 70' renewable-energy theme. As of year-end the manufacturing footprint comprised 9 manufacturing facilities in India plus 2 international subsidiaries (Nepal, Bangladesh) and 1 domestic subsidiary (Nerofix), supported by 112 depots and 8 regional distribution centres.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility
risks.note: The AR's Threats table flags that shifting trade dynamics, geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions can affect both availability and pricing of key raw materials - the single largest cost line for a paint maker, and the lever that decides whether pricing actions defend gross margin.

risks.risk: Trade restrictions, tariffs and logistics disruption on imported inputs
risks.note: Listed separately under Geopolitical and Macroeconomic Factors: trade restrictions, tariffs or logistical disruptions 'risk eroding cost competitiveness and supply continuity', i.e. a structural exposure of an import-dependent input basket rather than a one-off event.

risks.risk: Currency fluctuation and changes in import duties / quality control orders
risks.note: Classified as Financial Risk in the company's own risk taxonomy - 'results from currency fluctuations and market volatility, which can directly impact profitability'; the Threats page adds that changes in import duties, quality control orders and compliance standards feed straight into input costs.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition from new entrants and industry capacity expansion
risks.note: The Competitive Landscape threat states that new entrants and capacity expansion across the industry may increase pricing pressure - the structural de-rating risk for an incumbent decorative-paint franchise, since it caps realisations even when volumes hold.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity, system reliability and the DPDP Rules, 2025 compliance load
risks.note: System Risk is a named class in the risk framework ('increasing reliance on IT systems'), and the only Statutory Emerging Risk detailed is India's Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, which raise compliance obligations on personal data of customers, dealers and employees, with flagged impact of reputational damage and operational disruption from stricter data governance.

risks.risk: Water stress at manufacturing sites - water is both utility and raw material
risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table records water management as a Risk with negative financial implications because three KNPL manufacturing facilities sit in water-stressed regions and water is 'a vital raw material in the production of the Company's water-based paints'; the Threats page separately flags resource constraints affecting manufacturing continuity.

risks.risk: Climate transition: low-carbon regulation and cleaner-technology capex
risks.note: The sole Emerging Strategic Risk disclosed - long-term climate change, the transition to a low-carbon economy and emerging regulatory pressure - with the stated impact being investment requirements for cleaner technologies plus customer/stakeholder prioritisation of sustainable practices; managed under a TCFD framework. Extreme weather is also cited as a supply-chain and production-schedule risk.

one-line thesis: Kansai Nerolac delivered strong Q4 profitability despite crude and rupee volatility, driven by aggressive premium product launches and timely price hikes in decorative and industrial segments, with margin resilience and project business scaling to 10%+ of revenue — what matters is sustained margin discipline and leadership in high-margin niches amid inflationary headwinds.
financial scorecard: revenue: +7.6% YoY (standalone), +7.5% YoY (consolidated); EBITDA/margin: PBDIT +21% YoY (standalone), +30.6% YoY (consolidated) — margin expansion from mix shift and pricing; PAT (rptd): PBT before exceptional items +12.8% YoY (standalone), +23.2% YoY (consolidated); PAT (normalized): same as reported; order book: not disclosed; net debt: not disclosed — working capital improved via inventory focus, capex normal
guidance: revenue growth: implied mid-single digit to low double-digit for FY27; margin: targeting 13-14% EBITDA margin; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: capex normal and in line with prior years, no new capacity announced
segment / subsidiary detail: Decorative: mid-single digit growth, mix shifted to super-premium emulsions (Excel Everlast, Beauty Gold Washable Plus, Perma No Heat); Industrial: low double-digit growth in auto, mid-single digit overall; Powder & Performance Coatings: mid-single digit recovery; Project business: 10%+ of revenue; New businesses (waterproofing, wood finish): >10% of revenue
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of Nerolac Paint Plus zones (250+ stores); Architect/ID program (Illuminati) in 45+ cities; Painter network (1.2L+); Waterproofing and construction chemical verticals; Industrial growth via OE and channel in auto, CV, tractors, and coil coatings
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expansion driven by 7-8% cumulative price hikes in decorative (March-May), premium mix shift, and inventory cushion; industrial pricing lag partially offset by OE negotiation; sensitivity to 5-10% input cost rise partially hedged by pricing and inventory
capex / expansion: Capex normal and in line with prior years; no new capacity expansion announced; focus on efficiency and digitalization
capital allocation: Board recommended 250% dividend (INR 2.5/share); no M&A or buyback mentioned; reinvestment in R&D, branding, and retail infrastructure
risks & watch-items: West Asia crisis causing crude volatility and supply chain disruption; rupee depreciation increasing import costs; sustained high commodity prices; potential demand slowdown if inflation persists beyond 6 months; unorganized sector resilience
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined — prioritizing profitable growth over market share, emphasizing premiumization, pricing power, and margin resilience; cautious on near-term demand visibility but optimistic on structural trends; tone reflects leadership in innovation and ESG
non-obvious takeaways: Nerolac’s jingle is a 30+ year cultural asset driving brand recall; water-positive status and top 12% ESG ranking in chemicals is a rare differentiator; project business growth is now material (10%+) and scaling with marquee infrastructure wins; industrial pricing is being negotiated successfully despite B2B lag

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Kansai Nerolac Paints Limited (KNPL), a subsidiary of Kansai Paint Co., Ltd., Japan, is one of India's largest paint and coatings manufacturers, leading the Automotive and Powder Coating segments and ranked third-largest in Decorative paints.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: KNPL manufactures and supplies paints, varnishes, enamels, lacquers, wood coatings, construction chemicals and tile adhesives across Decorative and Industrial (Automotive, Auto Refinish, Performance/Powder Coating) segments. It serves residential, commercial, industrial, government, institutional and retail customers in India, with automotive coatings supplied to 2-, 3- and 4-wheeler, electric vehicle, commercial vehicle and tractor OEMs, and industrial coatings to consumer durables, machinery and infrastructure applications.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Kansai Paint Co., Ltd., Japan — holding: Parent and ultimate controlling entity; principal activity manufacturing paints; incorporated in Japan; ~74.96%-74.98% shareholding in KNPL
- KNP Japan Private Limited — subsidiary: Overseas subsidiary in Nepal; 68% shareholding
- Kansai Nerolac Paints (Bangladesh) Limited (formerly RAK Paints Limited) — subsidiary: Overseas subsidiary in Bangladesh; 55% shareholding; continued to face operating challenges during the year
- Nerofix Private Limited — subsidiary: Domestic (India) subsidiary; 100% shareholding; reported strong topline growth during the year
- Kansai Lanka Paints Pvt. Ltd. — subsidiary: Former overseas subsidiary in Sri Lanka; 60% shareholding; divested/liquidated during FY 2025-26 (period reported 1 Apr 2025 to 15 Dec 2025) amid macroeconomic challenges in Sri Lanka
- Kansai Paint Philippines Inc. — related party: Fellow subsidiary of parent KPJ; manufactures paints and related products in the Philippines; related-party sales counterparty
- Kansai Paint Asia Pacific SDN.BHD. — related party: Fellow subsidiary of parent KPJ; manufactures paints and related products in Malaysia
- Kansai Plascon Kenya Ltd. — related party: Fellow subsidiary of parent KPJ; manufactures paints and related products in Kenya
- Helios RUS LLC — related party: Fellow subsidiary; related-party sales counterparty (sale of finished goods/intermediates)
- Kansai Nerolac Paints Limited Provident Fund — related party: Post-employment benefit plan entity over which significant influence exists

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Decorative: mid-single digit growth, mix shifted to super-premium emulsions (Excel Everlast, Beauty Gold Washable Plus, Perma No Heat); Industrial: low double-digit growth in auto, mid-single digit overall; Powder & Performance Coatings: mid-single digit recovery; Project business: 10%+ of revenue; New businesses (waterproofing, wood finish): >10% of revenue

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Decorative:** Interior and exterior paints, Wood coatings, Construction chemicals, Tile adhesives
- **Automotive Coatings:** 2-, 3- and 4-wheeler coatings, Electric vehicle coatings, Commercial vehicle and tractor coatings, Underbody coatings, alloy wheel coatings, seam sealers
- **Auto Refinish:** Refinish coatings for premium A-class body shops
- **Performance Coatings:** Powder coatings, Liquid coatings, General industrial coatings
- **Other end-use coatings:** Consumer durables coatings (fans, microwaves, refrigerators, washing machines), Personal items coatings (hair clips, artificial jewellery), Transportation infrastructure coatings (bridges, metro rail)

growth_optionality.body: Expansion of Nerolac Paint Plus zones (250+ stores); Architect/ID program (Illuminati) in 45+ cities; Painter network (1.2L+); Waterproofing and construction chemical verticals; Industrial growth via OE and channel in auto, CV, tractors, and coil coatings

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian paints and coatings sector maintains a positive outlook, driven by infrastructure investments, increasing urbanisation, consistent automobile demand and rising consumer preference for premium products
- Geopolitical events expected to continue affecting crude oil prices, currency fluctuations and the global supply chain, though the industry is seen as well-positioned to manage these challenges
- Decorative segment faced near-term headwinds from geopolitical developments (Indo-Pak conflict impacting North region demand), an extended monsoon and a shorter festive cycle, with rural demand stable and urban demand showing gradual recovery through the year
- Automotive demand momentum strong across sub-segments, aided by GST 2.0-led affordability improvements, new model launches and festive-season tailwinds; Commercial Vehicles saw strong double-digit growth
- Electric Vehicle segment continues to see significant growth across mobility categories (two-wheeler, three-wheeler, passenger vehicle), reinforcing the Company's automotive-coatings leadership
- Performance Coatings demand supported by infrastructure development across railways, roads, airports and power projects, driving premium/high-end coating demand; General Industrial and Powder Coatings segments saw stable-to-healthy demand
- Auto Refinish benefiting from industry-wide transition from solvent-based to water-based systems and a customer shift toward premium products
- Project Business cited notable wins including the Jharkhand High Court and Raipur Vidhan Sabha projects

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expansion driven by 7-8% cumulative price hikes in decorative (March-May), premium mix shift, and inventory cushion; industrial pricing lag partially offset by OE negotiation; sensitivity to 5-10% input cost rise partially hedged by pricing and inventory

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Board recommended 250% dividend (INR 2.5/share); no M&A or buyback mentioned; reinvestment in R&D, branding, and retail infrastructure

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26, KNPL enhanced capacity at existing plants rather than adding new sites: water-based paints capacity was expanded at the Jainpur plant, and Cathodic Electro Deposition (CED) capacity was enhanced at the Sayakha plant, alongside internal initiatives to lift overall capacity through digital/automation investment. On the renewable-energy side, the Company commissioned a 2nd wind turbine of 2,100 KW capacity at Sayakha Plant, taking its captive windmill capacity to 10,500 KW (with windmill installations across Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat), and commissioned a 3,000 KW offsite captive solar farm in Yavatmal, Maharashtra, catering to power requirements at the Lote Plant — both pursued under the Company's 'Corporate RE 70' renewable-energy theme. As of year-end the manufacturing footprint comprised 9 manufacturing facilities in India plus 2 international subsidiaries (Nepal, Bangladesh) and 1 domestic subsidiary (Nerofix), supported by 112 depots and 8 regional distribution centres.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and disciplined — prioritizing profitable growth over market share, emphasizing premiumization, pricing power, and margin resilience; cautious on near-term demand visibility but optimistic on structural trends; tone reflects leadership in innovation and ESG

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the largest paint and coatings manufacturers in India; leadership in Automotive and Powder Coating segments and third-largest in Decorative
- Significant market share in performance coatings backed by deep technical expertise and longstanding industry partnerships
- Access to Kansai Paint Group's global technologies and R&D under the 'ONE KANSAI' cross-border collaboration initiative, aiding faster technology deployment and cost competitiveness
- In-house R&D capabilities via a state-of-the-art centre in Navi Mumbai plus satellite centres at manufacturing plants
- Extensive distribution network — 112 depots and 8 regional distribution centres across 28 states
- Strong retail engagement infrastructure: 150+ Nerolac NxtGen Shoppes, 250+ Shop-in-Shop units, 250+ Paint Zone touchpoints, and painter loyalty (Pragati) and influencer (Illuminati) programmes
- Diversified, balanced portfolio across decorative and industrial segments improving resilience across demand cycles

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: West Asia crisis causing crude volatility and supply chain disruption; rupee depreciation increasing import costs; sustained high commodity prices; potential demand slowdown if inflation persists beyond 6 months; unorganized sector resilience

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Nerolac’s jingle is a 30+ year cultural asset driving brand recall; water-positive status and top 12% ESG ranking in chemicals is a rare differentiator; project business growth is now material (10%+) and scaling with marquee infrastructure wins; industrial pricing is being negotiated successfully despite B2B lag

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strategy anchored in innovation, quality and customer-centric growth to strengthen the portfolio, enhance capabilities and respond proactively to evolving market needs
- Strategic focus centred on premiumisation, customer engagement, technology leverage and operational efficiency across a balanced decorative/industrial portfolio
- Leverage the Kansai Paint Group's global technologies and R&D through the group-wide 'ONE KANSAI' cross-border collaboration initiative for faster technology deployment and cost competitiveness
- Deepen painter/influencer/retail engagement via the Pragati Loyalty …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Services contribution] "Services is aiding the Primary business with Mid-Single-Digit % contribution of Decorative Business", delivered through Paas, AID and Pragati.
- [Segment growth commentary] Auto segment witnessed strong growth; powder coating witnessed robust growth with strength in Auto Ancillary, AC and Electrical and in Metallic Powders; PC liquid segment witnessed strong growth with strength in Construction Equipment, Drums & barrels and coil coating; Auto Refinish growth was flattish though with notable Bodyshop wins in Premium PU and a solvent-borne to waterborne conversion "transitioning as per plan".
- [Risk] Named risks are geopolitical conflicts leading to supply chain disruptions, high commodity prices due to high crude oil price and raw material availability uncertainty, and imports cost surge due to rupee depreciation.
- [Outlook] Per RBI, sustained demand from infrastructure and construction sectors; automotive demand to be buoyant driven by new launches and festive inventory build-up; consumer sentiment may get impacted due to the inflationary environment.
- [Q1 environment] The quarter's business environment was described as good demand in Automotive and government focus on infrastructure, against significant crude price increase, sharp depreciation in the rupee, geopolitical challenges and a delayed onset of monsoon.
